messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for host gpu-node-17 (rack-07). Alert: kernel panic + kubelet NotReady (autopager). Trigger: node-heartbeat-loss -> no kubelet heartbeats for 45s. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD12345

Sarah: acked oncall 10:32am. I'm attaching serial dump and starting triage.

Raj: on it. quick check: `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-17 -o wide` shows STATUS=NotReady, taints: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute. Any customer-facing pods?

Sarah: yes, 6 ML pods on that node (namespace=prod-models). Most are CrashLoopBackOff or Evicted. Tagging Olivia to confirm customer impact.

Olivia: looking at prod dashboards — 3 requests failing with 503s hitting the model-serving route that was pinned to this rack for low-latency. A/B fallback to dedicated pool hasn't fully kicked in for the canary tenant. Notifying support.

Miguel: grabbing serial console via IPMI/SOCAT to see kernel oops. Command: ```socat - /dev/ttyUSB0,raw,echo=0,nonblock,keepalive``` Serial output excerpt: 
```
[   24.512345] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
[   24.512389] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal GPU error
[   24.512400] CPU: 1 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/1 Not tainted 5.15.0-xxx
[   24.512412] Hardware name: SuperRack 2U
[   24.520000] ---[ end trace 0ba1c2d3 ]---
```

Raj: that looks like a driver/PCI-level GPU hang. Any NVMe errors too? those sometimes correlate.

Miguel: dmesg shows repeated nvme controller resets immediately before GPU error: `nvme 4: reset error, status: 0x40000`

Sarah: action plan: 1) mark node unschedulable (it's effectively down) 2) ensure eviction completed and workloads relocated to fallback pool 3) run a drain for any remaining pods 4) postmortem and RMA if hardware. I'll start the drain.

Olivia: support update sent to affected customers — told them we're failing over and expecting degraded latency for a few tenants while fallback warms. Ticket IDs: #SUP-7891, #SUP-7892.

Raj: running `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` now. Will watch for stuck pods.

Miguel: also capturing `nvme list` and SMART logs to include in postmortem. If NVMe is flaky, might have caused system instability that led to GPU fall-off.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert updated: gpu-node-17 escalated to SEV2 due to customer impact > 2 tenants. Escalation policy: infra-hardware + oncall-sre.

Sarah: pinging next oncall @next-oncall — handing off when Raj and I have eviction + initial diagnostics. ETA 20m for handoff.

next-oncall: acknowledged. I'll take lead for follow-ups and RMA coordination once you hand off. Please drop the diagnostics links.

Raj: most pods moved to fallback pool. 2 pods stuck in Terminating (CSI mount). Workaround: kill the kubelet container and re-apply; trying `kubectl patch pod ...` now.

Miguel: captured kernel oops (`/var/log/kern.log`) and uploaded to internal bucket: s3://redwood-debug/gpu-node-17/3790012345/ and added SMART logs.

Sarah: created incident doc (short) and added initial timeline + commands run. doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/gpu-node-17-3790012345. Outline: timeline, serial dumps, nvme SMART, pod impact, customer tickets, next steps (RMA, kernel/driver upgrade investigation).

Olivia: monitoring latency and error rates — routing fallback appears to have stabilized most tenants but canary still sees 10% overhead. Will continue observation and escalate to product if persists beyond 30m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by Sarah at 10:33am, assigned to group infra-hardware.

Sarah: handing off to @next-oncall at 10:52am. Raj and Miguel remain available for tech deep-dive. Leaving node cordoned and marked for RMA. Next steps for owner: coordinate RMA, validate nvme and GPU firmware, consider kernel/driver upgrade on fleet to mitigate similar fall-offs.

next-oncall: taking over. Thanks — I'll coordinate RMA and postmortem. Adding ticket to backlog and creating a follow-up task to review driver versions across the rack. :thumbsup: 

Olivia: support: customers notified of failover completion and updated SLA expectations. Closing support tickets pending final postmortem.

Sarah: resolving the pager in PD once handoff done. Leaving a note in the incident doc about the immediate mitigations. :white_check_mark: 

Raj: final note — if we see similar PCI fall-offs across multiple nodes, consider throttling NVMe IO during heavy model loads. Logging all kernel traces to help correlate.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved at 11:00am (status: handed_off).
